query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Atomic‐layer deposition of a dense Al₂O₃ film on boride‐based components will act as a diffusion barrier to molten aluminum, thereby reducing Al‐induced dissolution of the boride and formation of brittle intermetallics.
generation.material_initial_state: Uncoated boride‐based component (e.g. FeB coating on steel substrate) exposed to molten aluminum at 720 °C.
generation.intervention: Deposition of a 1–2 µm thick Al₂O₃ layer via atomic‐layer deposition on all exposed surfaces.
generation.conditions: Static immersion in 99.7 wt % Al at 700–750 °C for up to 100 h, with no mechanical abrasion.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, adherent, defect‐free Al₂O₃ coating.
generation.mechanism: The Al₂O₃ layer blocks Al atoms from contacting the boride, preventing dissolution of B and formation of Al–B intermetallic phases.
generation.predicted_outcome: At least 50% reduction in mass loss (from ~20 mg/cm² to <10 mg/cm² over 10 h at 720 °C) and no detectable Al penetration after 100 h.
generation.baseline: Uncoated boride components lose ~20 mg/cm² per 10 h in molten Al at 720 °C.
generation.boundary: Effective for exposures between 700 and 750 °C up to 100 h; effectiveness under cyclic thermal or mechanical stress remains untested.
generation.uncertainty: Long‐term coating stability under thermal cycling and mechanical abrasion is uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of boride‐based specimens: (1) with 1 µm ALD Al₂O₃ coating, (2) uncoated controls. Expose both groups to static molten Al (99.7 wt %) at 720 °C for 100 h.
measurements: Mass loss per unit area (mg/cm²) at 10 h intervals
SEM cross‐sectional imaging of coating/substrate interface
EDS mapping for Al content beneath the coating
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If coated specimens do not exhibit ≥50% lower mass loss than uncoated controls after 10 h, or if SEM/EDS shows Al penetration through the coating comparable to uncoated specimens, the hypothesis is falsified.
